flawed_step: Step 1: The required greedy-choice assertion—that every maximum-degree vertex can be chosen while preserving optimality—is unjustified and false.
counterexample: Let the graph be the path v1-v2-v3-v4-v5. Initially v2, v3, and v4 all have maximum degree 2, so choosing v3 is legal. This leaves the disjoint edges v1v2 and v4v5, forcing two further choices. The greedy output therefore has size 3, while {v2,v4} is a vertex cover of size 2.
assessment_summary: A legal tie-breaking execution of the maximum-degree greedy algorithm is not optimal, so the universal claim is false.
